The pole inequality is local near each interior point of D, includes -infinity on D, and does not impose a single boundary-uniform additive constant.
m log|zeta|^2 is a genuine negative psh competitor, so the pointwise supremum is nonempty.
The complex Hessian of -log(1-|w|^2) is delta/(1-|w|^2)+bar(w) tensor w/(1-|w|^2)^2, hence positive.
m log|zeta|^2+H_m is psh, negative because |zeta|^2<1-|w|^2, and has the required local pole bound.
Restriction to each normal disc is subharmonic or identically -infinity; the latter needs no comparison.
Off zero, subtracting m log|zeta|^2 subtracts a harmonic function; the pole bound gives an upper bound near zero, allowing the subharmonic removable extension.
On every inner radius r the finite part is <=-m log r^2; maximum principle bounds it inside r; r increases to R(w).

Admissibility gives the lower bound and fiber comparison gives the upper bound, so the unregularized supremum itself is exactly the formula.
H_m is bounded near every interior divisor point and the logarithmic term tends to -infinity there; elsewhere the formula is smooth.
The difference is only taken off D and extends as H_m, never evaluated as -infinity minus -infinity.
Phi_t is finite continuous, with a constant t neighborhood of D for each fixed t.
Zero is a competitor; the family is uniformly bounded by t; local upper-envelope theorem and continuity give psh V_t with 0<=V_t<=Phi_t<=t everywhere.
m log|zeta|^2+V_t is genuine psh, <=0 off D and -infinity on D, with the local pole bound because V_t<=t; exact G_m formula gives V_t<=H_m off D.
The normal-circle submean inequality for bounded psh V_t gives V_t(0,w)<=H_m(w), because H_m is independent of zeta.
a_t=1-exp(-t/m) lies strictly between 0 and 1.
F_t=-m log(1-a_t|w|^2) has Hessian m a_t delta/(1-a_t|w|^2)+m a_t^2 bar(w) tensor w/(1-a_t|w|^2)^2 >=0.
a_t<=1 implies F_t<=H_m, and ball membership implies H_m<=-m log|zeta|^2 off D; on D F_t<=t=Phi_t.
F_t is an admissible obstacle competitor, so F_t<=V_t.
H_m-F_t=m log(1+exp(-t/m)|w|^2/(1-|w|^2)); log(1+x)<=x yields the stated bound.
For each compact K in B, |w|<=R<1; the common exponential error yields uniform convergence on K including K intersect D.

At w_s=sqrt(1-s^2)w0 and zeta=as, ball membership is 1-(1-a^2)s^2<1 and G_m=m log a^2; a=exp(L/(2m)) realizes each finite L<0.
